source.title: Neural Functional Alignment Space: Brain-Referenced Representation of Artificial Neural Networks
source.authors: Rui Yan; Han-Qi Jiang; Yi Pan; Xiao-Bo Li; Tian-Ming Liu; Xi Jiang; Lin Zhao

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses convergence and reports model-to-brain alignment geometry, but it does not test whether representations of the same inputs become more similar across models as scale or capability increases.
record.gate_note: The study compares models using ROI-level encoding scores against fMRI responses, then compares those brain-referenced alignment profiles. It does not measure pairwise distances between models' representations of the same data points or relate such distances to scale or capability. Its geometric and SNCI results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version, not as tests of the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study builds brain-referenced alignment profiles (fMRI encoding scores per ROI) for 45 frozen models and clusters them. It never compares two models' representations of the same inputs and never relates any similarity to scale or capability. It cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis [18] only in passing, as motivation. Its 'cross-modal convergence' is shared brain alignment in the Limbic network, a different construct, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that NFAS shows modality-specific clustering of model-brain alignment profiles. They also report convergence in integrative cortical networks, which they say indicates shared computational constraints. They present representation dynamics (DMD stable mode) as a basis for brain-referenced model comparison.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses DMD-derived representations and fMRI ROI encoding scores to construct a brain-referenced model space; it does not use the original Platonic representation similarity method or test the original convergence claim.

fits_no_version.finding: Models' brain-referenced ROI alignment profiles cluster tightly by modality: PERMANOVA p<0.001, cosine distance 0.060 between modalities vs 0.0004 within, silhouette 0.995. The Limbic network shows relatively elevated SNCI alignment across all three modalities.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models of different modalities have modality-structured model-to-brain alignment profiles, with shared alignment in integrative (limbic) cortical systems.

record.problems: The reported comparisons are of brain-referenced alignment profiles rather than pairwise representations of the same inputs. The study does not relate its results to model scale or capability, and the cross-modal result is not based on paired image-caption inputs. Several network-level outcomes are stated qualitatively without numerical values in the text.

untested.parts: No model-model representational similarity, and no trend with scale or capability.
No paired image-caption alignment between vision and language models.
No mapping or stitching between models.
No feature or circuit recurrence across models.
No variation of the similarity metric or inputs for model-model convergence.
No test of plateau or causes of model-model alignment.

missing.what: Two-way ANOVA (modality × Yeo-7 network) on SNCI: significant main effects and interaction, all p<0.001. This supports R4/R5 but concerns only the brain-alignment construct.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation 'discusses' is overstated. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis appears only as a citation in the introduction, so 'cites_only' fits better. The paper's 'cross-modal convergence' refers to model-to-brain alignment, not model-to-model alignment. It should not be read as evidence for V1 or V2.

versions.untested_parts: No representation-similarity trend across model scale or capability is tested.
No alignment of vision and language representations on paired images and captions, or relation to model performance, is tested.
No comparison of same-architecture models across random seeds or shared features/subspaces is tested.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment between model representations is tested.
No recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models is tested.
The paper does not vary similarity metrics or input distributions for pairwise model-representation convergence.
The paper does not test whether pairwise representation convergence is incomplete, plateaus, or is explained by shared data or objectives.
